correctness.rationale: For each norm-one T an oriented edge molecule m has norm-one image. A vertex of the finite dual Lipschitz polytope attains the image norm and has integer values because its tight-edge graph is connected. If its value on m is ±1 it directly contributes numerical radius one; if zero, directed 0–1 arc shortest paths produce two 1-Lipschitz norming functionals summing to it. This yields 1≤2v(T) exactly, with all signs, endpoint cases and finite graph orders included. The published K3 formula supplies sharpness. The standalone checker independently verifies all 88,156 eligible decompositions on 771 graphs, but is explicitly not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The exact primary paper treats only three-point metrics, and the closest published all-graph theorem characterizes the index-one cases but does not bound indices of nonbipartite graphs. Other inspected all-dimensional or sharp examples cover only equilateral metrics or one wheel. The result requires an additional integer-potential splitting lemma, proved here for every finite unit-edge graph; the cited statements neither imply nor subsume it. Published-index and web alias/strength/parameter searches revealed no dominating bound. This remains a literature-based assessment, not a universal uniqueness certificate.
residual_risks: Equivalent results may be present in unindexed or unpublished literature under transportation-cost, root-polytope or graph Lipschitz terminology.
The published online comparisons had no independent audit status established here; only their actual scientific statements were used.

value.rationale: A universal dimension-free sharp lower bound across every finite connected unit-edge graph metric resolves a natural quantitative gap left by the index-one bipartite classification and scattered exact nonbipartite examples. The new directed shortest-path splitting lemma is structural and constructive. This is not a recomputation of a small table, a mere restatement of the equilateral case, or a claim of exact nonbipartite classification.
